The option set was wrong, and I was wrong in it. I claimed miter-inventory failed the no-policy test because it spawns git; it does not. git_extractor.rs:27 calls gaugeblock_git::Repository::discover, a grep for Command::new returns nothing, and its whole dependency list is gaugeblock-git, serde, serde_json, toml and thiserror. Moving it to common would place a foundation crate on top of a miter domain crate - an upward edge, the one direction the layer model forbids outright - so it cannot move until the AST vocabulary it consumes is itself extracted. Recommendation B would have shipped the crate that fails and kept the crate that passes, which is exactly backwards.

TRIAGE 2026-11-06. The four remaining allowlist entries are NOT vocabulary leaks and cannot be burned by repointing them at gaugeblock-contracts the way batten->contracts was. They are behavioral: the lower-layer product calls another product's engine.

  chalkline-core -> storypole-core   dag_compiler.rs uses add_task, link_tasks, CreateTaskParams, StorypoleStore. chalkline WRITES tasks.
  outfeed-core  -> sawhorse-core     synthesis.rs uses SawhorseConfig, RoleRouter, InferenceRequest, ModelRole, ReasoningEffort. outfeed CALLS inference.
  outfeed-core  -> storypole-core    storypole.rs uses add_task, verify_task, get_task_by_id, StorypoleStore. outfeed WRITES and VERIFIES tasks.
  dado-core     -> miter-polyglot    uses the AST vocabulary. This one IS a vocabulary leak, and MTR-22 is its prerequisite.

So the resolution per edge is dependency inversion, not relocation: the domain crate declares the port it needs and the integrator (-cli, which may depend on anything) supplies the implementation. Two edges share one seam each:
  chalkline-core declares a task-writing port; chalkline-cli implements it over storypole.
  outfeed-core declares an inference port and a task port; outfeed-cli implements them over sawhorse and storypole.
  dado-core waits on MTR-22.

Why this matters more than the count: an allowlist whose entries are behavioral will never empty by moving types, so a future reader repeating that attempt burns the same afternoon I just spent. The gate's meaning also changes - these entries say 'this product's engine is called directly from another product, and the fix is injection', which is a different sentence from 'this crate leaked a type'.

PROGRESS 2026-10-31. Four edges burned, 23 -> 19 lateral; allowlist 23 -> 19; downward edges 123 -> 130.

4. `joiner-core -> chalkline-core` - a DEAD coupling: one unused error variant, no other reference anywhere. Deletion, not refactoring.

THE CHEAP VEIN IS NOW EXHAUSTED, measured rather than assumed. A scan of every remaining edge for references outside `error.rs` returned non-zero for all of them (benchwork->storypole 9 files, chalkline->miter-engine 9, benchwork->sawhorse 6, joiner->dado 5, joiner->sawhorse 5, batten->dado 5, and 1 file each for joiner/miter-engine, dado/miter-engine, chalkline/storypole, outfeed/sawhorse, outfeed/storypole, benchwork/miter-engine). So none of the rest is a misplaced type or a dead error variant; they are genuine behaviour crossings.

What that leaves is design, in two shapes. (a) The benchwork decision below: 7 of the 19 edges are benchwork-core composing every other product. (b) Control inversion for the rest - chalkline writes tasks through `add_task`/`link_tasks`, outfeed queries tasks and records receipts, dado and joiner parse through the miter polyglot. Each needs a trait or CLI boundary rather than a move, and each is its own ticket-sized decision.

MEASURED 2026-11-06 (decision D1 raised, 0fa26f40). The 19 remaining edges are 135 import sites across 62 files, and they are three different problems, not one:

A. Already-paid moves, 7 edges: the symbols they reach for already exist in a foundation or split-out crate, so no inversion is needed, only a repoint. batten->dado 5 (TypedHole is in gaugeblock-contracts/src/dado_batten.rs), chalkline->miter-engine 12 (WorkspaceInventory, PublicTypeInventory and inspect_workspace are in miter-inventory), benchwork->miter-engine 4 (same), dado->miter-engine 3 (polyglot is miter-polyglot), joiner->miter-engine 3 (same, plus EngineError), plus the type halves of benchwork->sawhorse (ExecutionMode/InferenceRequest/ModelRole already in contracts::sawhorse, resolve_secret_from_env_file already gaugeblock_workspace::env_credentials) and benchwork->storypole (TaskNode, TaskStatus, TaskScope, EdgeKind, TaskDecision, DecisionStatus, HandoffPacket already in contracts::storypole).

B. Orchestrator by design, 7 edges: joiner->dado 9, joiner->batten 4, joiner->miter-harness 2, benchwork->chalkline 4, benchwork->joiner 4, benchwork->dado 3, benchwork->batten 2. joiner-core is the synthesis orchestrator and benchwork-core is the workbench hub; inverting these means rebuilding the crates whose purpose is composition.

C. Genuine control inversion, 5 edges: storypole (benchwork 23 behaviour sites, joiner 8, outfeed 6, chalkline 4) behind one BacklogPort, and sawhorse (joiner 10, benchwork 3, outfeed 4) behind one CompletionPort.

This corrects the exhaust-the-cheap-vein note above: that measurement predates the MTR-20 split, so it did not know miter-inventory and miter-polyglot now own the symbols chalkline, benchwork, dado and joiner reach for. Seven edges are still cheap.

Burn-down curve under option A: 19 -> 14 (the five repoints) -> 12 (the two type halves) -> 5 (declare the orchestrator layer) -> 2 (BacklogPort) -> 0 (CompletionPort).

miter-polyglot stays put: it constructs miter_ast::AstIndexer, FunctionSymbol, FunctionNode and Param (symbol.rs:42-91), so relocation would put foundation on top of a miter domain crate. MTR-22 carries the prerequisite; its two allowlist entries remain and are honest about why.

STEP 3 DONE 2026-11-06 (orchestrator layer). miter-analysis 487a313, harness a1499d1.

The layer is a named, documented list (ORCHESTRATORS = joiner-core, benchwork-core) because no name distinguishes a composition root from a product core. The admission criterion is narrow on purpose: composition must BE the product, not a step inside it - which is why outfeed-core and chalkline-core, both of which compose, stay domain crates and keep their edges gated. Those near-misses are written into the constant's docs so the next reader does not have to re-derive the line.

The change is stricter in the direction that matters: a domain crate importing a composition root was lateral and allowlistable before, and is upward - never excused - now. A test pins it.

HONEST CONSEQUENCE, larger than the 7 edges this step was scoped for: every orchestrator-to-domain edge clears, so 12 entries left rather than 7. In particular benchwork-core -> storypole-core (35 sites) and joiner-core -> sawhorse-core (13 sites) are now downward and ungated. A BacklogPort or CompletionPort there would still buy substitutability, but it is a quality goal, not a gate requirement, and the allowlist header says so rather than implying otherwise. The remaining plan is therefore 4 edges, not 7: chalkline and outfeed need the ports; benchwork and joiner no longer do.

One test encoded the old taxonomy (it used joiner-core -> dado-core as the example of debt) and was updated to use two crates that are still domain, with the reason in the comment.
